articles.title: In a first, British unmanned submarine Excalibur launches US heavyweight torpedo; why it matters
articles.summary: The Royal Navy’s 19-tonne XV Excalibur unmanned underwater vehicle has successfully launched a US-made Mk 48 heavyweight torpedo in a first-of-its-kind
articles.body: The Royal Navy’s 19-tonne XV Excalibur unmanned underwater vehicle has successfully launched a US-made Mk 48 heavyweight torpedo in a first-of-its-kind test.The US navy and Royal navy conducted the joint test on September 13 at the British Underwater Test and Evaluation Centre in Scotland under AUKUS Pillar 2.According to the US Navy, the trial was carried out under Project Broadsword and Trial Iron and was aimed at demonstrating whether a US heavyweight torpedo could be integrated with and launched from a British autonomous underwater platform.The test validated the mechanical, electrical and software integration between the weapon and Excalibur, which the Navy said demonstrated the ability of allied forces to achieve rapid weapon interchangeability.US chief of naval operations Admiral Daryl Caudle called it a “historic first for allied undersea warfare”, saying the successful launch demonstrated the allies' ability to integrate weapons and autonomous platforms.XV Excalibur and Mk 48 heavyweight torpedoThe XV Excalibur is the Royal Navy’s first extra-large uncrewed underwater vehicle (XLUUV), developed under the three-year Project Cetus programme.The 12-metre-long vehicle weighs around 19 tonnes and is designed as a testbed for advanced underwater technologies and payloads. The Royal Navy says Excalibur is intended to help develop future operations involving crewed and uncrewed systems working together.The weapon integrated onto Excalibur was the US Navy’s Mk 48 heavyweight torpedo, the US submarine force’s primary weapon for engaging enemy submarines and surface combatants.The torpedo is about 19 feet long, weighs roughly 3,500 pounds and carries a 650-pound high-explosive warhead, according to the US Navy. It is also capable of re-attacking a target if it misses during an engagement.Why it mattersThe test shows that unmanned underwater vehicles can potentially move beyond surveillance and carry heavyweight weapons.For future naval operations, armed XLUUVs could potentially extend underwater surveillance and strike capabilities while reducing the need to expose crewed submarines to certain missions.Integrating a US Mk 48 torpedo with a British autonomous platform also demonstrates how allied navies could build distributed, armed underwater capabilities without putting crews inside every launch platform.

articles.title: 'Manipulated the voter rolls': Mahua Moitra files police complaint against Gyanesh Kumar over SIR row
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: TMC MP Mahua Moitra on Thursday filed a police complaint against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at the Parliament Street Police
articles.body: NEW DELHI: TMC MP Mahua Moitra on Thursday filed a police complaint against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at the Parliament Street Police Station, alleging that the Election Commission "manipulated the voter rolls."Speaking to reporters, Mahua alleged that Kumar and the Election Commission's IT system had bypassed local officials responsible for maintaining electoral rolls.Her allegations came a day after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders related to the SIR."I have come today to the Parliament Street Police Station to file a complaint against chor Gyanesh Kumar, the Chief Election Commissioner of India, who has indulged in criminal conduct. What is the criminal conduct? The Election Commission is made up of three Election Commissioners to maintain checks and balances. Majority decisions prevail. It has now been proven by the Indian Express investigative report yesterday that two of the three Election Commissioners, namely Mr Joshi and Mr Sandhu, dissented from Mr Gyanesh Kumar's actions on 14 occasions in the last 10 months, and sometimes as many as four times in a single day," Mahua said."Very important things, such as the centralisation of the IT software, were left entirely in the hands of DG IT Seema Khanna, who was using this software to bypass local, on-ground officials. What is the rule? The rule is that in every Assembly constituency and at every booth, the local official, the ERO and the BLO, are in charge of the voter roll. What we find is that Seema Khanna and Gyanesh Kumar, by using the ECI software illegally and criminally, manipulated the voter rolls, bypassed these local officials and did not give them access to the system," she added.Moitra also alleged that the Election Commission made changes to Form 6, which is used to register new voters, without following the required procedure."Secondly, in terms of Form 6, Form 6 allows a person to register as a new voter. How does a new voter get enrolled by filling out Form 6? What Gyanesh Kumar did illegally was insert a new question into Form 6, which is: Are you or any of your parents or grandparents linked to the SIR, yes or no? Mr Sandhu and Mr Joshi dissented and said that only by amending the rules could you do this; you cannot simply add a question," she said."Nobody could answer. The CEO of West Bengal could not answer, and the Chief Election Commissioner could not answer, and lakhs and crores of new voters were left out. Today, all over India, 13 crore voters have been deleted. What will happen to their children? What will happen to their children when they turn 18? They cannot get on the rolls either. So this is criminal conduct, and they cannot hide behind Section 16 of the CEC and EC Act of 2023," she added.Later, after filing the FIR, Mahua shared a post on X along with a copy of the complaint. "Gyanesh Chor Kumar is rogue agent who acted without consent of other 2 ECs. Disenfranchising genuine voters is not official duties. He cannot enjoy immunity. He needs to be prosecuted. Simple," she wrote on X.According to the media report, the two Election Commissioners had objected to changes in Form 6, with Joshi and Sandhu recording that the statutory form could not be altered without amending the relevant rules. Sandhu later described the changes as “unauthorised and illegal” and called for their immediate removal.The ECI has maintained that written notes, observations and internal checks are part of normal institutional deliberations. It has also said that its official orders and decisions have full legal sanction and that final decisions, including those related to the SIR, were taken unanimously.The reported objections relate to voter registration and deletion, changes to Form 6 and centralised control of the electoral-roll database. According to the report, the two commissioners also raised concerns about access to the electoral-roll database by statutory officials.The reported differences have triggered demands from Opposition parties for action against Kumar. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi alleged that the BJP, RSS and the Election Commission had committed an act of “treason” through what he called “vote chori”."Vote chori is a crime against the Indian people and a direct attack on our Constitution," Rahul said. "The BJP, RSS and EC who organised it have committed an act of treason. Justice will be served."Mamata Banerjee also alleged that the BJP and the EC had “looted” the West Bengal Assembly polls and demanded fresh elections in the state using the voter list that existed before the SIR.Meanwhile, BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra defended the Election Commission, saying differences and exchanges between commissioners reflected “pure democracy” and were part of institutional deliberations.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: Nike cofounder Phil Knight just made the largest known donation to a public flagship university in the US.
articles.body: Nike cofounder Phil Knight just made the largest known donation to a public flagship university in the US. According to a New York Times report, Phil Knight and his wife Penny have donated a whopping $1 billion to the University of Oregon. The donation, surfaced from an unscheduled call, will go toward establishing an engineering college in the University. The latest pledge adds to previous donations by the Knights. Last week, they committed $1.1 billion to Providence St. Vincent Medical Center and Providence Heart Institute in Portland. In 2025, they gave $2 billion to OHSU’s Knight Cancer Institute. Knight, 88, has a net worth of nearly $23 billion, according to Bloomberg.Responding to the donation, Karl Scholz, president of the University of Oregon, told Fortune: “This extraordinary gift is an endorsement of what higher education delivers. It gives us the ability to scale innovation, accelerate impact, and meet the demand for skilled engineering required by the industries of tomorrow, all without placing that financial burden on state taxpayers.”Nike co-founder has given billions to Oregon causesThe couple has also made major donations linked to University of Oregon athletics. They have previously given $100 million to build the university’s basketball arena, named in honour of their late son, Matthew Knight.Phil Knight’s support has also helped create strong ties between the university and Nike. Oregon athletes have access to new and exclusive Nike gear, along with support related to name, image and likeness (NIL) deals. Because of the close relationship, some people call Oregon the “University of Nike.”Phil Knight’s donation comes as US university funding faces uncertaintyPhil Knights’ donation comes as federal support for universities faces uncertainty. In early 2025, the Trump administration laid off thousands of workers at federal science agencies, delayed some grant payments to universities and sought cuts to funding for research overheads. The administration also withdrew some DEI grants.Additionally, the White House’s fiscal 2026 budget proposal called for a nearly 36% cut in non-defense science research and development funding. articles.title: Poland says fire at Starlink station is sabotage as Denmark warns of rising Russian threat
articles.summary: The satellite station is used in part to provide internet coverage to neighbouring Ukraine, the government says.
articles.body:
A fire at a Starlink satellite station in central Poland was a deliberate "act of sabotage", the government has said.

Polish Deputy Prime Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said the fire in the Masovian Voivodeship province was "deliberately designed to disable the station... disrupting internet access for various institutions, including the Ukrainian army".

He told Polish public broadcaster TVP Info an investigation was ongoing but "many indications suggest" the attack fits into a "new Russian doctrine of attack". The Kremlin has not commented.

Meanwhile, Denmark's intelligence service issued a new threat assessment saying it expects Russia to escalate hybrid warfare in the coming months.

It said an attack remained "highly unlikely" but warned of "a low but growing risk" that Russia could launch a limited military attack against Nato countries.

In recent weeks a number of European Nato members have said Russia may be preparing attacks to test their commitment to supporting Ukraine, which Moscow denies.

Earlier this month, Germany blamed Russia for an attempted drone attack on Leipzig/Halle Airport , while France has ordered a plan to protect critical infrastructure and defence industry sites.

Hybrid warfare or hybrid attacks are loose terms which tend to describe non-military methods designed to exert pressure and destabilise an adversary - for example cyberattacks, sabotage or misinformation.

Proxies are often used to carry out the attacks and Russia always denies involvement, despite growing evidence to the contrary.

Europe targeted by spiralling campaign of sabotage - and Russia is the chief suspect

The fire at the state-owned Polish satellite station broke out on Wednesday night in Wola Krobowska. It remains operational.

The deputy prime minister said it transmits internet traffic through Poland to countries including Ukraine, and uses SpaceX systems that provide connectivity via Starlink terminals.

On Wednesday Poland also said a Russian military helicopter briefly violated its airspace , forcing it to scramble fighter jets.

Russian President Vladimir Putin has repeatedly said Moscow does not plan to attack Nato states.

Earlier this month, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said it was Europe speaking about preparing for war, adding: "If Europe attacks Russia, it will be a completely different war [from that in Ukraine], and it will be very short."

Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and Moscow currently controls about 20% of Ukrainian territory, including the Crimea peninsula annexed in 2014.

In Ukraine, Kharkiv and Kyiv experienced the worst of Russia's attacks overnight into Thursday.

In Kharkiv, six people were killed and twelve others injured in a Russian strike on a farm in the village of Stara Hnylytsia, Ukraine's state emergency services said.

It said they were agricultural workers sorting vegetables, with the head of the Kharkiv region adding that four were women.

In Kyiv, two people were killed and eight others injured overnight, emergency services said. More than 50 civilian facilities were also damaged in the city, including a maternity building.

The hospital's director said a woman gave birth to a baby boy in a shelter during that attack, adding: "Even on such a terrible night, life goes on."

Russia's defence ministry said it had hit Ukrainian defence facilities, logistics and telecom centres, as well as vessels used by the military.

Moldova's president said four Russian drones crossed into its airspace, with at least one exploding, while Romania's defence ministry said one drone crashed in its territory.

Russian aerial attacks on Ukraine have become more devastating in recent months because of their new jet-powered drones, which are harder to shoot down.

Kyiv is racing to develop low-cost weapons that can counter them as the missiles and fighter jets it has to fight them are too expensive.

Speaking at the UN General Assembly in New York on Wednesday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said, "we need ballistic interceptors to protect lives" and called on the US to help.

He said Putin needed to be stopped from continuing the war and "spreading this evil further", adding: "Putin is always looking for someone who can help him kill more, kill more people for every kilometre of land."

He said Ukraine would seek to target the Russian energy sector over the winter.

The Ukrainian president's comments came as Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev headed to the US to meet Trump administration officials, including Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, Reuters reported, citing two sources.

Russia's Lavrov told the UN Security Council on Wednesday there would be no pause in the war.

articles.title: 19-year-old cybersecurity researcher Nisarga Adhikary, who flagged flaws in CBSE portal, named in US DOJ Hall of Fame
articles.summary: Nisarga Adhikary, a 19-year-old cybersecurity researcher, receives recognition from the US Department of Justice for discovering vulnerabilities in the CBSE On-Screen Marking portal, showcasing his commitment to responsible disclosure and cybersecurity innovation.
articles.body: Nisarga Adhikary, a 19-year-old cybersecurity researcher who identified security vulnerabilities in the CBSE's On-Screen Marking portal, has been recognised by the US Department of Justice for responsibly reporting flaws in government systems.Adhikary announced the recognition on X, sharing a screenshot of the Justice Department's acknowledgements page. The page lists researchers who have reported valid vulnerabilities to the department through responsible disclosure.“Got added to US DoJ (Department of Justice) Hall of Fame,” Adhikary wrote.The recognition comes after Adhikary reported major security issues in the CBSE On-Screen Marking (OSM) portal, a digital system used by CBSE-affiliated schools to upload and manage students' examination marks. The platform forms part of the board's examination process and is used in the compilation of marks and preparation of results.The US Justice Department's Hall of Fame recognises cybersecurity researchers who identify vulnerabilities and help organisations address potential security risks.His interest in cybersecurity began with an early fascination with computers. Adhikary previously said he started exploring the field when he was around 13.“I have been fascinated by computers from a very young age, and I got into cybersecurity for fun when I was around 13. That curiosity gradually turned into something I wanted to pursue seriously,” he said.In June, IIT Kanpur appointed Adhikary as an Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT) and Threat Intelligence Engineer at C3iHub, the institute's cybersecurity-focused technology innovation hub.You use AI every day.
